overview: Pneumonia is an acute infection of one or both lungs that inflames the microscopic air sacs (alveoli). The alveoli may fill with pus and cellular exudative fluid, impairing oxygen exchange.
radiographic_findings: Focal or patchy alveolar airspace consolidation
Air bronchograms (patent airways surrounded by fluid-filled alveoli)
Silhouette sign (loss of normal anatomical borders, such as the hemidiaphragm or heart margin)
Lobar or segmental distribution of opacity
common_symptoms: Productive cough with greenish, yellow, or rust-colored phlegm
Shortness of breath (dyspnea) during routine activities
Sharp or stabbing chest pain aggravated by deep breathing or coughing (pleuritic chest pain)
Confusion or altered mental awareness, particularly in adults aged 65 and older
causes_and_risk_factors: Bacterial etiologies: Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, atypical pathogens (Mycoplasma pneumoniae)
Viral etiologies: Influenza virus, Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV), SARS-CoV-2
Risk factors: Age under 2 or over 65, chronic lung diseases (COPD, asthma), immunocompromise, tobacco smoking, aspiration risks
diagnostic_information: Posterior-Anterior (PA) and Lateral Chest Radiography (gold standard initial imaging)
Pulse oximetry to evaluate oxygen saturation (SpO2)
Complete Blood Count (CBC) showing leukocytosis with left shift
Sputum Gram stain and culture; blood cultures in hospitalized patients
treatment_approaches: Targeted empirical antimicrobial therapy based on outpatient vs. inpatient stratification (e.g., macrolides, beta-lactams, fluoroquinolones)
Adequate oral and intravenous hydration to loosen pulmonary secretions
Supplemental oxygen therapy if SpO2 drops below 92-94%
Fever management with antipyretics and supportive pulmonary toileting
when_to_seek_care: Persistent difficulty breathing or breathing at an abnormally rapid rate
Cyanosis (bluish tint to lips, nail beds, or skin)
Acute confusion or severe lethargy in elderly patients

reliable_sources.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
reliable_sources.title: Pneumonia: Symptoms, Causes, and Clinical Guidelines
